Why Premium Natural Fabrics Win the Weekend
When you are relaxing on a Sunday afternoon, the fabric sitting against your skin dictates your entire mood.

If you are sitting on a sunny outdoor patio, synthetic fabrics are going to make you sweat immediately. Pure cotton breathes naturally. It allows air to circulate right through the garment, keeping you feeling fresh and cool while you sip your coffee.

Linen is honestly the king of daytime style. Yes, it wrinkles slightly as you wear itâ€”but that is actually the beauty of the fabric! Those soft, natural creases give off a highly sought-after, premium vacation vibe that works perfectly for a relaxed weekend meetup.
Unlike stiff fast-fashion garments, our natural fabrics are pre-washed. They feel incredibly soft and broken-in the very first time you put them on, saving you the hassle of a rigid break-in period.

How to Care for Your Weekend Wardrobe
Take care of your premium Cottonworld pieces, and they will be your go-to weekend gear for years.
1. Cold Washes Only: Always wash your cotton and linen in cold water. Hot water can break down natural fibers and fade those brilliant summer colors.
2. Inside Out: Turn your shirts and trousers inside out before tossing them in the machine. It protects the fabric's face and keeps the buttons from chipping against the drum.
3. Avoid the Dryer: High heat is the enemy of a great fit. It ruins elastane and shrinks cotton. Always air dry your weekend wear on a line or a good hanger in the shade.
4. Embrace the Steam: For linen shirts, don't worry about getting a perfectly crisp press. Just run a steamer over the fabric to drop the heavy wrinkles, and let the natural texture shine through.
Ready to upgrade your weekend rotation? Mix and match our premium everyday essentials below:
1. Is a T-shirt acceptable to wear to brunch?

It totally depends on the venue! For a casual neighborhood spot, a high-quality, perfectly fitted plain T-shirt paired with clean chinos or premium shorts is a great look. Just avoid old, faded graphic tees. If the restaurant is a bit nicer, step up to a polo or a casual button-down.
2. Should I tuck my shirt in?

For daytime weekend events, untucked is usually the way to go. It keeps the vibe casual. Just ensure the hem of your shirt isn't too longâ€”it should land right around the middle of your back pocket. If you are wearing a polo with chinos to a nicer spot, you can certainly tuck it in for a cleaner silhouette.
3. Why do people wear linen during the day?

Linen is highly breathable and pulls heat directly away from your body. Because brunch usually happens during the warmest parts of the day (late morning to early afternoon), linen keeps you significantly cooler than heavier fabrics while looking incredibly stylish.
4. Can I wear dark colors during the day?

While pastels and light neutrals are traditional for daytime, a dark navy or olive green works perfectly year-round. Just try to avoid wearing an entirely black outfit in the middle of a hot, sunny day, as it will absorb heat and look a bit too heavy for a relaxed weekend event.
5. Are shorts okay for a nice restaurant?

Yes, but they must be the right kind of shorts. Athletic wear, swim trunks, or baggy cargo shorts are usually a no-go for nice restaurants. However, a pair of our tailored, flat-front chino shorts paired with a collared linen shirt and loafers is a completely acceptable, highly sophisticated summer outfit.
